Its ToR indicates that employees and pensioners can expect final recommendations, the fitment factor and the revised pay structure soon.  Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 4 Nov 2026, 11:15 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google The 8th pay commission has completed 66% of its tenure timeline, employees and pensioners can await final recommendations, fitment factor and revised pay structure. ( 8th pay commission ) AI Quick Read One year after being commissioned, the 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) has now completed around 66% of its tenure. In a post on its official social media account, the panel said that employees and pensioners can await the final recommendations, including the fitment factor and revised pay structure. The Commission's decisions are expected to benefit over 1 crore people, including around 50 lakh central government employees and close to 65 lakh pensioners, including defence and railway personnel and retirees. Chaired by former Supreme Court Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai , with Pankaj Jain, a former IAS officer, as Member-Secretary, and Professor Pulak Ghosh, a tenured Professor of Finance and Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister as Member of the Commission, the panel is required to announce its recommendations within 18 months of its constitution. Also Read | DA hike: Tamil Nadu, MP, Rajasthan—States with Diwali dearness allowance hikes Fitment factor, revised pay — What to expect? The Terms of Reference ( ToR ) of the 8th CPC outline what central government employees and pensioners can expect from its final recommendations. Approved by the Union Cabinet last year, the ToR defines the Commission's scope of work and specifies the areas on which it must make recommendations. The panel is expected to examine and recommend changes that are desirable and feasible in the emoluments, including: Pay (usually includes salary structure, pay matrix) Allowances (usually include DA, Dearness Relief, HRA) Other facilities/benefits, in cash or kind (includes increments, promotions, etc.) Consider rationalisation, contemporary functional requirements and specialised needs Also Read | DA arrears: Punjab HC issues contempt notice, orders compliance affidavit 8th CPC: What has happened so far? Notably, official meetings started in March, while windows for data and suggestion submissions closed in July. Views and input gathered from stakeholders such as employee unions, labour groups, ministries, pension bodies, and others will be analysed to inform the final recommendations on allowances, the pension formula, and salary structures. While the Commission did not release an agenda for the visits, these meetings are expected to feature discussions and deliberations on several recurring themes raised during discussions and in memorandums submitted by prominent unions. These unions and groups collectively represent a large number of employees and pensioners, including defence and railway staff. The meetings are significant, as discussions with representatives are expected to play an important role in shaping the commission's deliberations. Also Read | 8th Pay Commission: How arrears will be paid after recommendations, explained When can we expect 100% timeline? The ToR for the 8th CPC states that recommendations are to be announced within 18 months of the panel's constitution. Thus, the absolute deadline to submit the report is May 2027 . Once the pay commission's recommendations are made, the rollout could take another two to three years to complete. This means that hikes announced in 2027 may only be fully implemented by 2029 or 2030.
